Jordan (Acme Corp): Heads-up — we toggled our account to use the int8 cost profile for embeddings and now some requests return a shorter vector and similarity is way off.
Jordan (Acme Corp): Sample response we got: 
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "request_id": "rq_02ABCDEF",
  "model": "open-embed-bert-768",
  "embedding": [0.023, -0.112, ...],
  "embedding_length": 384
}
Jordan (Acme Corp): Expect 768 dims. This started immediately after applying profile "int8-performance" from Console. Cosine top-1 scores fell from ~0.93 to ~0.67 for our test set.
Jordan (Acme Corp): Repro: 1) POST /v1/embeddings model=open-embed-bert-768, batch_size 8 2) Hosted API 3) Applied profile in Console 4) Received rq_02ABCDEF

alice (Support): thanks for the details, @Jordan. Can you paste the exact curl and the request_id you showed? Also confirm hosted vs dedicated/private.

Jordan (Acme Corp): Hosted. curl: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-bert-768","input":["how to optimize infra"],"max_batch_size":8}'
```
Request id: rq_02ABCDEF.

alice (Support): forwarding to eng-runtime. Quick checks while they look: try max_batch_size=1 or force precision=fp16 to see if dims restore. Also try explicit header X-Redwood-Model if Console variant pinning is allowed.

Jordan (Acme Corp): Tried max_batch_size=1 -> still 384. Switched profile back to fp16 in Console -> dims back to 768 and similarity recovered. So it's tied to the int8 profile selection.

sam (eng-runtime): pinged — thanks. Initial triage: our catalog maps quantization profiles to model variants. Two likely failure modes: 1) profile incorrectly resolving to a different variant with a smaller projection head (e.g., 384), 2) runtime quantization kernel truncating output when running int8 path under specific batching patterns. I'll pull the request logs.

sam (eng-runtime): sanitized trace: 
[2026-02-03T09:12:04Z] recv rq_02ABCDEF
[2026-02-03T09:12:04Z] catalog.resolve(profile=int8-performance, model=open-embed-bert-768) -> open-embed-bert-384-int8
[2026-02-03T09:12:04Z] selected kernels: int8-dyn-cpu
[2026-02-03T09:12:04Z] produced output shape (1,384)

sam (eng-runtime): That catalog.resolve line is the smoking gun — the alias matched a smaller variant. The profile should not change final embedding size; it should only alter precision/quantization of the identical-arch variant. Looks like an alias collision after a recent catalog update.

Jordan (Acme Corp): So the profile should never swap projection dimension. We only clicked the int8-profile for the 768 model in Console.

sam (eng-runtime): Correct. This is a bug in alias resolution: int8-performance was linked to tags that include both 768 and 384 variants and our selector logic favored lower-memory variants for performance labels. We'll patch to require exact model id match before falling back to tag-based aliasing.

alice (Support): temporary mitigation: pin exact variant in Console (open-embed-bert-768@v2) or set header `X-Redwood-Model: open-embed-bert-768@v2` to force the 768 projection until fix is live. If you want int8, we can enable it only on the pinned variant and monitor.

Jordan (Acme Corp): Pinning fixed it immediately. Thank you. We want to try int8 if quality is close — what's realistic quality delta between fp16 and int8 for embeddings?

sam (eng-runtime): High-level guidance: fp16 should be nearly identical to fp32 aside from tiny numeric noise. int8 may shift embedding geometry more; small deltas are expected, but it should not change the dimension. Typical avg cosine delta depends on model and calibration; for this family we usually see 0.01-0.03 avg drop after a well-calibrated int8 conversion. Always validate with at least a few hundred sample pairs.

sam (eng-runtime): Planned fix: 
- update alias resolution priority to prefer exact model id
- add integration test that ensures embedding_length == expected_dim for any profile application
- add metric and alert if >0.1% of requests have embedding_length != expected_dim for a model

eva (SRE): creating INC-2026-0054 to track. Rolling config patch to catalog service; will canary in us-east1 first. ETA canary 30m, full 3h if green.

deploy-bot: started deploy catalog/20260203-alias-fix to canary (us-east1)
deploy-bot: canary health ok after 8m
deploy-bot: rolling out to remaining regions

eva (SRE): rollout complete. Added temporary log-level alerting to detect any stragglers.

sam (eng-runtime): patch merged. New selector requires model id match before applying profile alias; also added a compatibility check that blocks profile application if the profile would switch final projection dims without explicit user confirmation.

alice (Support): Jordan, you can now re-enable int8 on the pinned variant; we'll watch the new metric for any dimension drift. If you'd like, we can run a quick Optimize eval run across 1k pairs to quantify the FP16 vs INT8 delta for your data.

Jordan (Acme Corp): Re-enabled int8 on open-embed-bert-768@v2 and ran 1000 eval pairs. Avg cosine delta ~0.019, top-1 recall drop negligible for our use case. Looks acceptable. Please send ticket summary and assign follow-up.

alice (Support): Ticket SD-2026-4499 created. Summary: catalog alias bug allowed profile alias to resolve to smaller projection model, causing embedding dimension mismatch and quality regressions for some hosted customers after enabling int8-performance. Fix: tighten alias resolution, integration test + metric, compatibility gating for profile application, rollout complete. Workarounds: pin variant or use fp16. Follow-up: Optimize team will add explicit compatibility/preview step in Console for cost-saving profiles.

Jordan (Acme Corp): Thanks. Please cc morgan@acmecorp.com on the follow-up.

alice (Support): Will do. We'll keep monitoring for 24h then close if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
